taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Anatherum glomeratum. Andropogon glomeratus is retained as the primary familiar alias because Texas field guides and local floras still overwhelmingly use it.
look_here_first: BUSHY BLUESTEM (Anatherum glomeratum): the official USGS true var. glomeratus flowering closeup NOW illustrates dense brushes of many clustered short, pale-silky racemes and leafy upper sheaths. Compare broomsedge's more separate narrow spathe-sheathed racemes, big bluestem's open turkey-foot, and historical Hawaiian var. pumilus now under A. tenuispatheum. Confirm intact raceme pair, spathe and sessile/pedicellate spikelets under magnification; photo gross architecture alone is not specimen-proof.

project_inclusion.range_basis: UT Plant Resources Center North Hays County long-term grassland account; documented Travis County LBJ Wildflower Center occurrence; detailed Williamson County species treatment under synonym Andropogon glomeratus.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Synonym-based county records are counted only because Kew explicitly treats Andropogon glomeratus as a synonym of Anatherum glomeratum.

best_field_traits: Tuft-forming perennial, usually with upright stems and relatively narrow blades.
Dense, oblong to bushy crown produced by many tightly crowded short branches and silky raceme pairs.
Look within the fluff for leafy spathe-like bracts subtending the short paired racemes (often 1.5–3 cm).
Rachis joints and pedicels carry long whitish hairs that expand into a silvery or cottony mature head.
Moist grasslands, ditches and drainage edges support the hypothesis but are not diagnostic.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: BUSHY: broad, dense cottony tuft of many short paired hairy racemes and small sheathlike spathes. BROOMSEDGE: generally narrower, more separated individually spathe-enclosed units. LITTLE: many short silky racemes on separate branches, but not one densely packed brushy terminal head. BIG: 2–6 exposed relatively stout turkey-foot racemes. KR: several longer, more separate slender terminal fingers; confirm mature paired spikelets before a management decision.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Bushy bluestem forms a densely crowded oblong tuft of many short silky paired racemes, each arising with a spathe-like bract. Broomsedge has more separated, narrower spathe-sheathed pairs; little bluestem has shorter individual silky racemes borne on distributed leafy upper branches; big bluestem has relatively stout digitate turkey-foot fingers; KR has more slender longer clustered fingers, not the dense tuft.

field_id_finish_pass.first_clue: Brush-like, densely crowded white-haired seedhead composed of MANY small paired raceme units, instead of the few stout open fingers of big bluestem.
crew_field_sequence: Photograph the whole rooted bunch and upper stem before disturbing the crown.
Look closely at the upper flowering cluster. A compact, often oblong cottony brush suggests bushy bluestem.
Part the crown with fingers to find paired 1.5–3 cm racemes subtended by small leafy spathe-like structures.
Compare flowering-unit placement: broomsedge's units are more individually separated; little bluestem's short units are on many upper leafy branches; big bluestem's thick fingers are exposed.
Photograph the leaf collar plus mature spikelet pairs at 10–20×. Without those views, keep difficult stems at Anatherum sp. rather than treating them as confirmed bushy bluestem.

immediate_lookalikes.cue: Broomsedge: narrower, more elongated inflorescence with short hairy racemes individually more enclosed by spathe-like sheaths.
Little bluestem: separate short, silky racemes among branched upper culms, not one very crowded brushlike inflorescence.
Big bluestem: open turkey-foot with relatively stout racemes, typically 2–6 near culm tip.
KR: long, relatively slender exposed fingers in a terminal group; overall density and individual raceme structure differ.
Cane bluestem: pronounced beard of hairs at culm nodes; verify node and raceme morphology, not head color.
Silver bluestem: cottony silvery reproductive cluster; distinguish by head architecture and spikelets, not white hairs alone.

IMPORTANT CURRENT POWO SPLIT (2026): Andropogon glomeratus (unranked binomial) is synonym of Anatherum glomeratum, but Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus is synonym of a SEPARATELY ACCEPTED species, Anatherum tenuispatheum. This makes old Hawaiian var. pumilus photo records unsuitable as A. glomeratum species-example evidence. A. tenuispatheum also differs from A. virginicum (Andropogon virginicus). Never collapse these three canonical installed species or recertify county nativity from image names. Review A. glomeratum existing county PASS separately; its recorded Williamson County is outside project target zone.

vegetative_broomsedge_vs_bushy.source: Hagenbuch & Lemke 2015 Phytoneuron 2015-4 pages 26,34 (PDF indices 25,33), Texas Hill Country living and herbarium specimens
vegetative_broomsedge_vs_bushy.first_character: On fresh sheaths inspect the shape and WHICH margin has hairs. Bushy often laterally compressed/keeled with pilose open margins; broomsedge is VARIABLE and may also have conspicuous margin/collar hairs. This is NOT a safe binary species diagnosis. Compare flowering architecture and calibrated spikelets.

vegetative_matrix.bushy: Typically laterally compressed and keeled; conspicuously broader than the blade
vegetative_matrix.broomsedge: Typically rounded, keeled just below collar; lower sheaths sometimes flattened and keeled

vegetative_matrix.bushy: Texas Hill Country treatment: both open margins pilose; hair amount can vary and photo positioning matters.
vegetative_matrix.broomsedge: Texas Hill Country treatment: often nearly entire, sometimes outer ciliate; other regional sources explicitly document long margin/base hairs, so NOT reliably hairless. Both margins must be imaged.

vegetative_matrix.bushy: 1–2 mm, membranous, truncate, ciliate or with longer hairs
vegetative_matrix.broomsedge: 1–2 mm, membranous, truncate, with short and long cilia — NOT diagnostic from a single fuzzy fringe
2–5 mm, overlap; width alone cannot confirm

vegetative_matrix.bushy: Many units crowded into a broad brush
vegetative_matrix.broomsedge: More spaced units partly held by narrow enclosing spathes

vegetative_matrix.bushy: Need same-voucher 1 mm intact paired sessile/pedicellate spikelet image; hairs alone overlap
vegetative_matrix.broomsedge: Need same-voucher 1 mm paired spikelet and bract details; avoid relying on winter color

vegetative_broomsedge_vs_bushy.critical_photo_gap: Leaf/sheath micro PHOTO gap: need matched correctly determined living Texas specimens, one photo to prove inner opened SHEATH margin and a second to prove outer SHEATH margin, then the true collar/ligule and ruler. Existing USGS broomsedge leaf/stem photos show some hairs near the sheath, but neither is yet proven to show both identifiable margins with enough resolution. University/extension photos with unclear public reuse rights must not be installed.

source_caution.summary: IMPORTANT REVISION (2026-10-22): Do NOT key bushy versus broomsedge as simple 'hairy sheaths = glomeratum, hairless = virginicum'. The 2015 Texas Hill Country key describes hair on the distinct/open bushy sheath margins and generally entire broomsedge margins, sometimes with cilia on the outer edge. However Missouri, Texas A&M and Oklahoma sources explicitly show or describe broomsedge sheath or leaf-base hairs too. Species, growth stage, which margin is imaged, and geographic treatment can change the apparent difference. Inspect actual UPPER sheath shape and both separated margins on the SAME confirmed plant; treat hairs as one supporting character only. Big mature flowering architecture and measured rames/spikelets remain needed for confident separation.

diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.look_here_first: Bushy bluestem: find a DENSE oblong brush of many short, silky PAIRED racemes tucked among leafy spathes. Part the head and follow ONE 15–30 mm raceme pair back to its spathe, then inspect a 3–4.5 mm SESSILE fertile spikelet and its reduced PEDICELLED partner. Overall white fluff is only the first clue.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.growth_form: Warm-season caespitose perennial; GrassBase culms approximately 75–150 cm, leaves 2.5–6 mm wide. Photograph the attached rooted clump and upper flowering crown; wet ditch habitat is supporting context, not proof.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.ligule_collar: True ligule is a short ciliolate membrane; Go Botany gives approximately 0.6–2.2 mm for Andropogon glomeratus sensu its treatment. Texas Hill Country vegetative account gives about 1–2 mm, with hairy edges. Photograph opened upper sheath, BOTH margins, true membrane and scale. Broomsedge can also have sheath hairs; neither hair presence nor ligule length alone separates them.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.paired_racemes_and_spathe: Flowering units typically two short 15–30 mm sinuous racemes paired within a 15–30 mm spatheole; densely grouped to form an oblong brush. Rachis joints and curved pedicels are silky. The fertile spikelet is SESSILE; the companion PEDICELLED unit may be reduced to a barren pedicel. Do not arrow a presumed fertile pedicellate spikelet from an unresolvable photo.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.spikelet_glumes: Mature sessile fertile spikelet approximately 3–4.5 mm. Lower glume about spikelet length, with two lateral keels and concave interkeel face; upper glume one-veined and awnless. Glumes exceed the delicate floret. Photograph actual separated glumes in front/side view with 1-mm scale; no numerical glume lengths independent of spikelet length were established by these sources.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.lemma_awn: Fertile lemma thin, apically bifid with ONE awn arising between lobes; GrassBase awn approximately 10–20 mm, and Go Botany 6–19 mm under its treatment. Awn belongs to the SESSILE fertile lemma, NOT the hairy rachis or glume. Lower floret is sterile; palea absent or minute. Require same-specimen dissection before labeling awn insertion.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.local_lookalikes: Anatherum virginicum (broomsedge): more separated, narrower spathe-sheathed silky racemes; do not rely on sheath hairs. Anatherum tenuispatheum: distinct accepted taxon; old Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus Hawaiian media are NOT valid bushy-glomeratum evidence. Schizachyrium scoparium: silky racemes distributed among upper branches, not a compact brush. Andropogon gerardi: a few stout open turkey-foot branches. Bothriochloa ischaemum (KR): separate slender terminal fingers; compare real paired spikelets for management decisions.
last_mile_photo_arrow_gaps: Same vouchered Central Texas rooted bushy plant: complete flowering crown and attached upper sheath/spathes, centimeter scale; preserve source-locality evidence separately from county-native certification.
Part one true raceme PAIR inside its spatheole, show both 15–30 mm racemes and attached hairy rachis/pedicels with 1-mm ruler.
At 10–20× show SESSILE fertile 3–4.5 mm spikelet and actual reduced PEDICELLED companion; arrows only after source pixels distinguish attachment.
Dissect same sessile spikelet: lower two-keeled glume, upper one-veined glume, bifid fertile lemma and awn emerging from sinus, all with 1-mm scale.
Open the TRUE collar and both sheath margins on the same plant; measure ciliolate membrane and compare confirmed broomsedge at matching scale.
Do not repurpose quarantined Hawaiian var. pumilus photographs or unknown-rights extension images as glomeratum anatomical evidence.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.public_ready_criteria: Keep FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until same-specimen diagnostic paired racemes, sessile/pedicelled structure, glumes/lemma/awn origin and true ligule are visually verified at adequate scale, source identity and individual public-use rights checked, arrows placed only on visible anatomy, and public learner QA passed. Preserve existing images/rights, 2026 species-split hold and county-range flags; no nativity recertification.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.evidence_scope: Measurements are literature ranges for the accepted species/historical Andropogon glomeratus synonym, not newly verified on existing archived photographs. No taxonomy or target-county status changed.

lane3_photo_evidence_reconciliation_2026.photo_arrow_rule: Retain gross-structure arrows on existing source-confirmed photos. Do not infer sessile versus pedicellate structures from silky bulk photo.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK FOR THE BUSHY BRUSH
field_id_short_tiles.short: Many short silky paired racemes crowd into a broad oblong crown
field_id_short_tiles.details: Bushy bluestem is a tufted perennial with erect culms often about 75–150 cm in Kew GrassBase. Numerous crowded short flowering units make a broad, cottony terminal brush, unlike broomsedge's more separated spathe-held units. Texas Uvalde whole-clump and USGS flowering photographs show this gross architecture; a white head alone is not definitive.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · PART THE SPATHES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Find paired 1–3 cm rames inside short leafy spathe-like sheaths
field_id_short_tiles.details: Look within the fluffy mass for short paired racemes, commonly about 1.5–3 cm, partly subtended by small leafy spathes. The silky hairs arise prominently from rachis internodes and pedicels. A whole flowering head does NOT expose each spathe boundary or a measured raceme pair; obtain a connected specimen and 1-mm ruler before placing anatomy arrows.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN THE TRUE COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: A short ciliate membrane, not merely long sheath-margin hairs
field_id_short_tiles.details: The actual ligule is a short ciliolate membrane at the inner blade–sheath junction; the USFS bushy bluestem treatment describes it at about 1 mm. Sheaths can be flattened/keeled and may carry hairs on their margins, but broomsedge can also have sheath hairs. Open BOTH margins and expose the true ligule beside a 1-mm scale. Existing photographs do not prove these microscopic features.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · FIND THE FERTILE SESSILE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: Ripe sessile spikelet roughly 3–4.5 mm; partner reduced or absent
field_id_short_tiles.details: Kew GrassBase describes a 3–4.5 mm fertile sessile spikelet; the USFS treatment gives about 3–4 mm. Its pedicelled partner is usually strongly reduced or absent, leaving a silky-haired pedicel. Separate the two firmer enclosing glumes: the lower has two lateral keels; the upper has one mid-keel and is awnless. Glumes approximately reach or exceed the enclosed florets. Do not arrow a hair tuft as a pedicelled spikelet.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · LOCATE THE REAL LEMMA AWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: One straight awn from the cleft fertile lemma, usually 10–20 mm
field_id_short_tiles.details: Inside the glumes is a sterile lower floret with a thin lemma and an upper fertile floret whose hyaline lemma has a bifid tip. A SINGLE slender awn arises from the notch (sinus) of the fertile lemma, about 10–20 mm in Kew GrassBase; the USFS account gives about 10–15 mm. The awn is not a glume extension. A detached, scaled fertile lemma and awn insertion are still missing.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · CHECK THE LOCAL BLUESTEMS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Broad bushy brush ≠ broomsedge's separate units or little bluestem
field_id_short_tiles.details: Anatherum virginicum has more individually separated narrow spathe-held units, although sheath hairs overlap. Schizachyrium scoparium has distributed short silky racemes; Andropogon gerardi has stout exposed turkey-foot fingers; KR bluestem has longer slender clustered fingers. Historical Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus photographs belong to separately accepted A. tenuispatheum, NOT this species: gallery panel 6 is OTHER-species comparison only. Never infer county-native PASS from the Uvalde photo.

Published descriptions, not measurements demonstrated by archived images.
